claim: Google Threat Intelligence's Agentic platform uses two specialized agents divided by task domain — a general Threat Intel (CTI) Agent and a dedicated Malware Analyst Agent for file-based reverse engineering — rather than one monolithic agent.
stance_target: Triggers/Infrastructure pillar — specialized department agents (akin to Director/Worker or specialized-team pattern) in a production security product
scope_conditions: Google Threat Intelligence Enterprise/Enterprise Plus license tier, production system
quoted_support: Specialized Agents: the platform uses agents optimized for specific tasks, such as the Threat Intel Agent for general queries and the Malware Analysis Agent for file-based investigations.

claim: The platform explicitly surfaces raw tool-call outputs to the user as a deliberate hallucination-detection mechanism, described as helping the user and the system 'generate new improved prompts specifically attempting to prevent further hallucinations.'
stance_target: Zero-Hallucination & Quality Control pillar — exposing intermediate tool-call evidence (not just final answer) is a concrete production anti-hallucination design pattern
quoted_support: This information for helping detecting hallucinations to consequently generate new improved prompts specifically attempting to prevent further hallucinations.

claim: Even with RAG grounding and inline citations, the vendor explicitly warns that generative AI 'may sometimes produce inaccurate information' and tells users to treat responses as a starting point, not a final verified answer.
stance_target: Zero-Hallucination & Quality Control pillar — vendors acknowledge that RAG + citations does not achieve true zero-hallucination, undermining absolute claims
quoted_support: While powerful, the generative AI may sometimes produce inaccurate information. Always use the provided responses as a starting point for your investigation and double-check critical information.

claim: The Malware Analyst Agent performs deep reverse engineering across multiple binary formats (PE, ELF, Mach-O, .NET assemblies, AutoIt3-compiled scripts) and deobfuscates scripts (VBA, PowerShell, HTA, JavaScript) to recover C2 servers and encryption keys, as a documented production capability.
stance_target: Reverse Engineering & Codebase Mastery pillar — concrete named capabilities a production security agent performs on decompiled/obfuscated code
scope_conditions: Google Threat Intelligence Malware Analyst Agent, production
quoted_support: Script & Macro Deobfuscation: Can analyze and deobfuscate various script formats (VBA, PowerShell, HTA, JavaScript), unrolling stagers and recovering encryption keys or Command and Control (C2) servers within a file.

claim: Responses in the platform cite sources split into two categories — internal GTI database resources and external Web resources — displayed in a dedicated Sources panel, as a verifiability mechanism.
stance_target: Zero-Hallucination & Quality Control pillar — structured source attribution (internal vs external) as a verifiability design pattern for agent answers
quoted_support: This side panel displays the references used to generate the answer, organized into two sections: GTI (resources from the Google Threat Intelligence database) and Web (external global resources).
